prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Labour’s 2005 manifesto sets out a progressive, reforming programme to take Britain forward, not back: extending opportunity and security for the law‑abiding majority, rejecting the false choices between economic dynamism and social justice, and matching rights with responsibilities.

Record since 1997: Stable growth, low inflation and interest rates, 2m more in work, rising living standards, fewer children and pensioners in poverty; major investment and reform in NHS and schools; crime down 30%; free museums; doubled aid and leadership on climate.

Economy and jobs: Keep disciplined fiscal and monetary rules; no rise in basic or top income tax; targeted help for families and work incentives; aim for full employment (80% employment rate), higher minimum wage, active welfare-to-work and incapacity benefit reform; back enterprise, science and skills; smarter regulation; strong financial services; modern energy policy (renewables, efficiency, a balanced mix); £180bn+ transport investment with rail, road and urban transit upgrades and road-pricing debate.

Public services: Services free to all, personal to each. Put power in the hands of patients, parents and citizens; more GPs, nurses and community services; community hospitals; foundation trusts; independent and voluntary providers where they add capacity at NHS standards; maximum 18 weeks from referral to treatment by 2008; tougher action on hospital infection; dentistry reform.

Education: Personalised learning from early years to 19; every secondary a specialist school; 200 Academies by 2010 focused on low‑aspiration areas; Building Schools for the Future; stronger discipline; more vocational excellence with 14–19 diplomas, apprenticeships and FE reform; fair access to higher education with no upfront fees, a £3,000 cap, more bursaries, and a 50% participation aim.

Crime and security: A neighbourhood policing team for every community; firm action on antisocial behaviour; expand drug testing and treatment; Serious Organised Crime Agency; tougher rules on guns and knives; stronger sentencing and offender management; better support for victims and witnesses.

Migration and borders: A fair, firm system that benefits Britain—points‑based migration prioritising skills and English; civil penalties for illegal employment; faster, fairer asylum; biometric visas, e‑passports and ID cards to strengthen security and tackle fraud.

Families and older people: Halve child poverty by 2010–11; universal affordable childcare and Sure Start in every community; longer paid maternity leave and more flexible work; expand homeownership and shared ownership; Pension Credit to combat poverty now, and a cross‑party consensus on sustainable pensions; more choice and independent living in care.

Housing, communities and equality: More and better social housing and choice‑based lettings; cleaner, safer neighbourhoods; advance equality with a Single Equality Act and a new Commission; balance rights with responsibilities.

Britain in the world: Engage to keep Britain strong and the world fairer—lead in the EU (with a referendum on the Constitutional Treaty), NATO as cornerstone, modern armed forces and retained nuclear deterrent; support democracy, ME peace; meet 0.7% aid by 2013, cancel debt, promote fair trade; global climate leadership (Kyoto+, emissions cuts).

Democracy and devolution: Complete Lords reform; devolve further to nations, regions and councils; empower neighbourhoods and social enterprise; keep council tax under control.

Quality of life: Broaden participation in culture and sport; 2012 Olympic legacy; modern libraries; digital switchover; strong, independent BBC; cleaner local environments and a Marine Act.

The social contract: we help you, you help yourself—spreading opportunity, demanding responsibility, and securing justice for all.
